messages:
From: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@medicore.com>

Date: 2026-11-30T09:14:00Z
Subject: Quick Qs on where requests actually run (EU)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great visibility in the console. Before we take this to our security review, two quick clarifying questions from our infra/compliance team: 1) For inference requests originating in the EU, can you enumerate exactly which subprocessors might see the request payload or the cached artifacts (KV / prefix caches) during handling? 2) If we pin to a Redwood Dedicated cluster in eu-west-1, are there any automatic cross-border hops (e.g., control plane telemetry, metrics ingest, backup trajectories) to the US or other regions we should expect?

If you have a simple table or diagram mapping request hops (ingress -> execution -> caching -> telemetry -> retention), that would be ideal. We may need this for our DPA appendix.

Appreciate it — Lucia
Lucia Gomez
Head of Platform Security, Medicore Health

-----

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@medicore.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-30T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where requests actually run (EU)

Hi Lucia — thanks for the thoughtful questions. High level answers up front, then I attached a short matrix and a simple hop diagram for the team.

1) Subprocessors that may touch inference payloads (EU origin):
  - Redwood Dedicated (customer-owned GPU pool) — execution remains in the pinned region when pinned; no compute hops by default.
  - Cloud storage provider for optional persistent caches (if enabled) — we can pin to an EU storage bucket; by default Redwood uses regional buckets.
  - Monitoring/telemetry vendor (metrics/alerts) — by default metrics are aggregated to our control plane; we can configure EU-only metrics endpoints for Dedicated customers on enterprise plans.
  - Logging snapshot store used for post-mortem evidence (short TTL) — configurable, default retention 7 days, can be routed to customer-managed storage.

2) Control plane and telemetric metadata:
  - Control plane (control signals, rollouts, auth) is a separate plane and may originate from the US for some accounts. For Medicore we can enable the Private control plane option or a Dedicated control-plane routing to ensure control-plane metadata remains in EU.
  - By default there are no customer PII-containing payloads forwarded to the US for EU-pinned Dedicated inference; however anonymized telemetry/aggregates may flow cross-border unless you opt into EU-only telemetry.

Attached: redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v2.pdf (subprocessor roles + EU routing), eu-data-sojourns-diagram.png (simple hop diagram), and a checklist for evidence.

Next steps: Kar, Marissa — can you add the EU-only telemetry config notes and a short line on retention SLA for transient caches? Lucia — I can schedule a 30-min call with our infra team if you want to walk through the diagram.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
-----

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@medicore.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-30T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where requests actually run (EU)

Thanks Jordan — added a few clarifications from the operations side and copied the specific retention numbers in the attached spreadsheet. Short notes below:

- Transient KV/prefix caches: default TTL = 2 hours; configurable down to session-only (ephemeral) for Dedicated. No persistent copies are made unless customer enables caching.
- Persistent cache (optional): we recommend EU object storage; default replication kept in-region. If customer requests cross-region replication for DR, that's an opt-in and appears in the DPA amendment.
- Logging snapshots: retained for 7 days by default, can be extended per contract (30/90/365 days), and we can route snapshots to customer-managed EU storage for long-term retention.
- Telemetry: request-level metadata used for routing and SLOs; by default aggregated metrics (no raw prompts) are sent to our control plane. For Medicore we can enable EU-only telemetry ingestion (Enterprise feature, needs control-plane routing).

Attachment: scp-evidence-checklist.xlsx (evidence items, recommended artifacts to attach to procurement ticket). Happy to hop on a call to walk through.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
